mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the CPIAUCSL annualized growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past month signals a robust consumer-driven economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases & UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% over the past quarter, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 2% and GDPC1 growth < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 over the past month signals a strong labor market, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with an increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months signals accommodative monetary policy supporting housing demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases & HOUST increases in 2 months
regime_hint: monetary easing with housing demand growth
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS decreases and HOUST increases.
